newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fernandez sees Argentine Q2 GDP up at least 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fernandez sees Argentine Q2 GDP up at least 5 pct.

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, in an interview with Reuters, forecast the Argentine economy will grow by at least 5.0 percent in the second quarter from the similar 1996 period.
The growth is smaller than the 8.1 percent level reached in the first quarter, but the economy early in the year rebounded from a weak base in January through March of 1996.
"The economy is recovering strongly, more than we expected," Fernandez said. "We calculate the economy will grow by at least five percent in the second quarter."
He reiterated an official upward revision in the growth forecast for 1997 to six percent from five percent earlier this year. He said that could be even higher.

"We always try to give conservative numbers because we don't want to give false expectations," he added. "We rose around eight percent in the first quarter so we now revised it and think it (the annual rate) could be more than six percent.
The minister added that economic strength could generate a 1997 trade deficit higher than the $1.5 billion that was expected earlier in the year.
"The projections for imports and exports are strengthening and as there is strong foreign direct investment the trade deficit could be wider."
